content.title: About
content.content: Cornbread prepared from mix (2572) is a classic American quick bread made primarily from cornmeal. It has a dense yet crumbly texture, a golden crust, and a subtly sweet, buttery flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cornbread originated in the United States in the 19th century as an easy way to use cornmeal.
Traditionally baked in a rectangular pan, it also appears as muffins or mini loaves.
The mix usually includes leavening agents, salt, sugar, and powdered milk for convenience.
In the Southern states it is commonly served with fried meat, beans, and barbecue sauce.
Cornbread can be sweetened with honey or sugar, or made savory with cheese or herbs.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Cornmeal provides slow‑releasing energy, helping to keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and regular bowel movements.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B3 and folate aid carbohydrate metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Provides magnesium and iron
items.content: These minerals are important for muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: Low in gluten
items.content: For those sensitive to gluten, cornbread can be a more tolerable option, though it is not completely gluten‑free.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Cornbread can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared mixes often contain added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve warm, sliced, as a side to soups, stews, fried meats, or vegetable dishes. Spread with butter, honey, or jam, or use it for sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the baked bread in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate up to a week or freeze wrapped tightly.
